observations.explanation: The paper reports 101 multi-app workflow tasks among 369 Ubuntu tasks and describes substantial annotation effort, repeated cross-checking, and quality-control rounds (PDF pp. 6–8). The claim is appropriately scoped to the benchmark and its construction.

The human study reports 72.36% overall performance, compared with baseline agent success rates far below that level (PDF pp. 9–11). This supports a meaningful measured capability gap on this benchmark.

The authors explicitly state that further red-teaming could reduce false positives and negatives, leaving this for future work (PDF p. 8). This supports the qualified concern about residual evaluator error risk.

The paper identifies the 369-task main benchmark as defined and executed on Ubuntu and separately reports 43 Windows tasks (PDF p. 6). Calling the suite Ubuntu-centered and Windows supplementary is justified.
